{{Infobox election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin, 2018 | country = Wisconsin | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = All eight Wisconsin seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = 5 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 3 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsWI}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the eight [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Wisconsin]], one from each of the state's eight [[Wisconsin's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]]. The Wisconsin Partisan Primary will be held on August 14, 2018 with the Governor, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, odd-numbered Wisconsin State Senate seats, and all Wisconsin Assembly seats on the ballot.{{Cite web|url=http://elections.wi.gov/node/4813|title=2018 Partisan Primary {{!}} Wisconsin Elections Commission|website=elections.wi.gov|language=en|access-date=2017-12-27}} {{Toclimit|limit=2}} ==District 1== {{see also|Wisconsin's 1st congressional district}} The 1st congressional district is located in southeastern [[Wisconsin]], covering [[Kenosha County, Wisconsin|Kenosha County]], [[Racine County, Wisconsin|Racine County]] and most of [[Walworth County, Wisconsin|Walworth County]], as well as portions of [[Rock County, Wisconsin|Rock County]], [[Waukesha County, Wisconsin|Waukesha County]] and [[Milwaukee County, Wisconsin|Milwaukee County]]. The district's current Representative is [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]], [[Paul Ryan]], the current [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|Speaker of the House of Representatives]], who was the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] candidate for [[Vice President of the United States]] in the [[United States presidential election, 2012|2012 U.S. presidential election]]. The district's [[Partisan Voter Index]] is R+5, indicating a slight Republican lean. Ryan could potentially have seen a close race; in hypothetical polling, his main Democratic challenger, [[Randy Bryce]], was behind Ryan by only seven points. Ryan was also facing challenges in the Republican primary from [[Paul Nehlen]], who also challenged Ryan in 2016, and from Nick Polce. Ryan announced on April 11, 2018, that he is not seeking re-election. On April 22, Bryan Steil, member of the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents and former personal driver to Ryan, announced his bid for the seat, with news outlets reporting Steil as the Republican Party nominee front-runner.{{cite web|url=http://host.madison.com/wsj/news/local/bryan-steil-becomes-gop-front-runner-to-win-paul-ryan/article_adc01853-d11c-5500-96da-0bdd1c144c89.html|title=Bryan Steil becomes GOP front-runner to win Paul Ryan's seat|publisher=Wisconsin State Journal|date=April 22, 2018|accessdate=April 22, 2018}} Two Democrats have announced; ironworker [[Randy Bryce]] and [[Janesville, Wisconsin|Janesville]] school board member Cathy Myers. ===Democratic primary=== ;Nominee * [[Randy Bryce]], Ironworker, union activist{{cite web|url=http://host.madison.com/wsj/news/local/govt-and-politics/racine-area-ironworker-democratic-activist-launches-bid-to-unseat-paul/article_2b0ee469-56b9-5ae1-91d8-4fd4763a2431.html|title=Racine-area ironworker, Democratic activist launches bid to unseat Paul Ryan|work=[[Wisconsin State Journal]]|last=Sommerhauser|first=Mark|date=June 19, 2017|accessdate=June 19, 2017}} ;Eliminated in primary * Cathy Myers, [[Janesville, Wisconsin|Janesville]] School Board member (endorsed Randy Bryce){{cite web|url=http://www.gazettextra.com/news/fellow-janesvillian-wants-to-challenge-rep-ryan/article_a045996b-e17a-507f-b9d6-7f52883f1bd5.html|title=Fellow Janesvillian wants to challenge Rep.
